Chapter 6: The Quiet Years—Leadership from the Shadows.
There’s a moment in every journey when things just... slow down. The world outside gets quieter, and the noise fades away. For Amy, those later years at Dohnavur brought a stillness she’d never really known before. You might think being mostly bedridden after her injury would have ended her influence. But for Amy, it was actually the start of something new—a fresh way to lead, to love, and to serve, even from the sidelines.
Imagine her in that small, sunlit room, watching the life of the community go by. She could hear children laughing in the courtyard, workers chatting softly as they took care of their daily chores, and somewhere in the distance, the gentle hum of prayer and song. Sure, her body was weaker, but Amy’s mind? Still sharp as ever. And her heart? Every bit as engaged.
Instead of walking the grounds, Amy wrote letters—hundreds of them. Each one was filled with encouragement, advice, and sometimes a gentle nudge in the right direction. Her words kept their warmth and conviction, just like when she was able to be everywhere at once.
There was this young woman, new to Dohnavur, who really struggled with the weight of responsibility. She constantly worried she’d never live up to Amy’s example. Then, one afternoon, she found a simple note slipped under her door: “You are not called to be Amy. You are called to be yourself, faithful in the small things.” Simple, right? But those words lifted a huge burden. It’s amazing, isn’t it, how a few honest words can completely change someone’s outlook?
Amy’s leadership during these years was almost invisible—quiet, in the background. She listened more than she spoke, trusted others to make decisions, and let go of controlling every little detail. That’s when it became clear: true influence isn’t about being at the center. It’s about empowering others to grow. The community learned to lean on each other, share the tough stuff, and celebrate even the smallest victories.
Of course, there were tough times too. Illness swept through the home more than once, and resources were stretched pretty thin. But the spirit of Dohnavur held strong, shaped by the values Amy had woven into every corner—humility, compassion, and that fierce commitment to caring for the vulnerable. Even as her own strength faded, Amy’s vision shone brighter than ever.
Looking back, those quiet years weren’t a decline at all. They were a time for deepening. Amy discovered that love doesn’t depend on staying busy or racking up achievements. It’s found in showing up, in praying, and in letting others take the spotlight. The seeds she’d planted so long ago kept growing, quietly and steadily, in the lives of everyone she touched.
